newsitem.title: UK: London gold price strides upward.
newsitem.headline: London gold price strides upward.

text.p: Gold extended a vigorous advance on Friday afternoon, shaking off its laggard status against a rally in the other precious metals seen since the beginning of the year.
It traded almost $10 higher than on Thursday, close to $355 per ounce.

Hopes that the yellow metal would join the rally by silver, platinum and palladium prices had been crushed under fears that fresh sales of bullion might be made by central banks to raise money to meet financial rules for European Monetary Union.
More pertinently, as the gold price fell the market felt the weight of gold producers borrowing gold to sell in order to protect their profit margins from ever declining prices.
But buying of physical gold in the Middle East and Asia has provided a floor for the price as consumers there took advantage of low prices ahead of, for example, the Chinese New Year.
That support for a price above last week's 3-3/4 year low at almost $336 per ounce encouraged the speculative investment funds to cover bearish short positions and sparked a rebound.
Gold fixed at $353.30 in London on Friday afternoon versus $350.75 in the morning and $345.00 on Thursday.
A move higher was widely forecast, although dealers saw limits on the move.
"I would not be bullish for it over $355.00," one said.
Part of the new enthusiasm behind gold buying came from a comment from South African Reserve bank governor Chris Stals on Thursday.
Stals said he doubted if recent sales from the Dutch and Belgian central banks would be followed elsewhere.
But several market analysts were dismissive of the opinion stressing that this could be seen as a palliative for South African miners and exactly what the gold market wished to hear.
"You could see something behind this if the European Monetary Union (EMU) had been postponed," one analyst said.
Doubts about Russia's Norilsk nickel-platinum-palladium complex to continue normal production amid labour, management and financial problems helped raise platinum group metal prices.
Platinum was indicate at $370.80/$371.80, its highest price of the year and palladium was at $136.75/$137.75 - steady although below a fund-driven 11-month high struck on February 13 of $141.25.
